unit_of_record: One published study (a paper). n_patients counts patients within it; same_patient_as links papers describing the same patient.
inclusion_criteria: A serious psychiatric syndrome resolved or substantially improved.
The resolution was incidental: the triggering event or treatment was aimed at something else, or not aimed at all.
Individual patients or small series; lesion series allowed when built on individual cases.
Discoveries that were unexpected when reported but are established since stay in, labelled 'Known now'. Findings that later failed controlled testing are labelled 'Refuted'.

Antique section: cases first observed before 1970, sorted by observed_year (the year of the original observation, which can predate the citation). Period diagnoses are accepted as written, resolution may be narrative, and follow-up may be missing; such records carry the flag antique-bar. Deliberate exposures (E3) and secondary syndromes resolving with their cause (E4) are still excluded, except that the incidental founding observation behind a later deliberate therapy is eligible. Each antique record carries historical: the diagnosis in the period's own terms, a likely modern reading, and why it is worth reading.
